title: Minimum Number of Increasing Subsequence to Be Removed
summary: Given an array of integers, you can repeatedly remove any strictly increasing subsequence.
statement: Given an array of integers, you can repeatedly remove any strictly increasing subsequence. Determine the least number of such operations needed to empty the array.
constraints: nums is a nonempty integer array and may contain duplicates.
Each operation removes any strictly increasing subsequence of remaining elements.
Return the minimum operations required to remove every element.
hints: Partitioning a sequence into strict-increasing chains needs as many chains as the longest non-increasing subsequence.
Negate values and compute the longest nondecreasing subsequence with patience sorting and bisect_right.
Insert -x at upper_bound in tails; the tails length is the answer.
Dilworth’s chain-antichain theorem gives equality, while patience sorting computes the obstructing non-increasing length including duplicates.
editorial: Dilworth’s chain-antichain theorem gives equality, while patience sorting computes the obstructing non-increasing length including duplicates.

tests.explanation: A non-increasing subsequence 5,3,1 has length three, forcing three rounds; three increasing chains achieve it.
The entire array is strictly increasing and can be removed in one operation.
